sanskrit: ādityo 'yaṃ sthito mūḍhāḥ snehaṃ kuruta mā bhayam bahurūpo muhūrtaś ca jīvetāpi kadā cana
english: "The sun yet stands in the sky, you fools — show your love and do not be afraid. The hour takes many forms; perhaps even now the child may yet revive."

sanskrit: yūyaṃ bhūmau vinikṣipya putrasnehavinākṛtāḥ śmaśāne putram utsṛjya kasmād gacchatha nirghṛṇāḥ
english: "Having laid him upon the ground, stripped of all love for your son, why do you abandon the boy at the cremation ground and go away so pitilessly?"

sanskrit: na vo 'sty asmin sute sneho bāle madhurabhāṣiṇi yasya bhāṣitamātreṇa prasādam upagacchatha
english: "Have you no tenderness for this son, this sweet-spoken child, by the mere sound of whose speech you would melt into delight?"

sanskrit: na paśyatha sutasnehaṃ yādṛśaḥ paśupakṣiṇām na yeṣāṃ dhārayitvā tān kaś cid asti phalāgamaḥ
english: "Do you not see how strong is the love for offspring even among beasts and birds, though from rearing them no profit ever comes to them?"

sanskrit: catuṣpāt pakṣikīṭānāṃ prāṇināṃ snehasaṅginām paralokagatisthānāṃ muniyajñakriyā iva
english: "For four-footed creatures, for birds and insects, for all beings bound by affection, this love is, in its bearing on the world beyond, like the sacrificial rites of sages."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ putrābhirāmāṇām iha loke paratra ca na guṇo dṛśyate kaś cit prajāḥ saṃdhārayanti ca
english: "For these creatures that delight in their young, no advantage is seen either in this world or the next — and yet they go on sustaining their offspring."

sanskrit: apaśyatāṃ priyān putrān naiṣāṃ śoko 'nutiṣṭhati na ca puṣṇanti saṃvṛddhās te mātāpitarau kva cit
english: "When they no longer behold their beloved young, no grief abides in them; nor, once grown, do those offspring ever nourish their mother and father in return."

sanskrit: mānuṣāṇāṃ kutaḥ sneho yeṣāṃ śoko bhaviṣyati imaṃ kulakaraṃ putraṃ kathaṃ tyaktvā gamiṣyatha
english: "Whence then this love among men, in whom grief is destined to dwell? How will you forsake this son, the very perpetuator of your line, and go your way?"

sanskrit: ciraṃ muñcata bāṣpaṃ ca ciraṃ snehena paśyata evaṃvidhāni hīṣṭāni dustyajāni viśeṣataḥ
english: "Long shed your tears, long gaze upon him with love; for things dear as these are, above all, hard to give up."

sanskrit: kṣīṇasyāthābhiyuktasya śmaśānābhimukhasya ca bāndhavā yatra tiṣṭhanti tatrānyo nāvatiṣṭhate
english: "Of one fallen low, hard-pressed, and facing the cremation ground, where the kinsmen take their stand, no stranger will stand beside him."

sanskrit: sarvasya dayitāḥ prāṇāḥ sarvaḥ snehaṃ ca vindati tiryagyoniṣv api satāṃ snehaṃ paśyata yādṛśam
english: "To every creature its own life is dear, and every creature comes to know love; behold how strong is the love of the good even among the beasts of the wild."

sanskrit: tyaktvā kathaṃ gacchethemaṃ padmalolāyatākṣakam yathā navodvāhakṛtaṃ snānamālyavibhūṣitam
english: "How can you abandon and go from this boy, with his long, lotus-restless eyes, adorned as for a fresh wedding, bathed and decked with garlands?"

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca jambukasya vacaḥ śrutvā kṛpaṇaṃ paridevataḥ nyavartanta tadā sarve śavārthaṃ te sma mānuṣāḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Having heard the jackal's words of piteous lamentation, all those people then turned back for the corpse's sake.

sanskrit: gṛdhra uvāca aho dhik sunṛśaṃsena jambukenālpamedhasā kṣudreṇoktā hīnasattvā mānuṣāḥ kiṃ nivartatha
english: The vulture said: Ah, shame! Addressed by this cruel, dull-witted, base little jackal, O men of feeble resolve, why do you turn back?

sanskrit: pañcabhūtaparityaktaṃ śūnyaṃ kāṣṭhatvam āgataṃ kasmāc chocatha niśceṣṭam ātmānaṃ kiṃ na śocatha
english: "Forsaken by the five elements, empty, reduced to the state of a mere log and devoid of motion — why do you grieve for him? Why do you not rather grieve for your own selves?"

sanskrit: tapaḥ kuruta vai tīvraṃ mucyadhvaṃ yena kilbiṣāt tapasā labhyate sarvaṃ vilāpaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati
english: "Practice fierce austerity, by which you may be freed from sin. By austerity all things are won; what will lamentation accomplish?"

sanskrit: aniṣṭāni ca bhāgyāni jānīta saha mūrtibhiḥ yena gacchati loko 'yaṃ dattvā śokam anantakam
english: "Know that fortunes, with their embodied forms, are unwelcome too, whereby this world passes on, bequeathing grief that has no end."

sanskrit: dhanaṃ gāś ca suvarṇaṃ ca maṇiratnam athāpi ca apatyaṃ ca tapomūlaṃ tapoyogāc ca labhyate
english: "Wealth and cattle and gold, gems and jewels too, and offspring — all are rooted in austerity, and through the practice of austerity are won."

sanskrit: yathākṛtā ca bhūteṣu prāpyate sukhaduḥkhatā gṛhītvā jāyate jantur duḥkhāni ca sukhāni ca
english: "As it has been wrought, so among beings is their measure of joy and sorrow attained; a creature is born already having taken up its sorrows and its joys."

sanskrit: na karmaṇā pituḥ putraḥ pitā vā putrakarmaṇā mārgeṇānyena gacchanti tyaktvā sukṛtaduṣkṛte
english: "Not by the father's deeds does the son fare, nor the father by the son's; by separate paths they go, each leaving behind his own good and evil works."

sanskrit: dharmaṃ carata yatnena tathādharmān nivartata vartadhvaṃ ca yathākālaṃ daivateṣu dvijeṣu ca
english: "Practice righteousness with diligence, and likewise turn back from unrighteousness; and conduct yourselves, each in due season, toward the gods and toward the twice-born."

sanskrit: śokaṃ tyajata dainyaṃ ca sutasnehān nivartata tyajyatām ayam ākāśe tataḥ śīghraṃ nivartata
english: "Cast off grief and wretchedness, and turn back from love of your son. Let him be abandoned to the open air, and then return at once."

sanskrit: yat karoti śubhaṃ karma tathādharmaṃ sudāruṇam tat kartaiva samaśnāti bāndhavānāṃ kim atra hi
english: "Whatever good deed a man does, and whatever dreadful unrighteous deed, the doer alone reaps it; what part have kinsmen in this?"

sanskrit: iha tyaktvā na tiṣṭhanti bāndhavā bāndhavaṃ priyam sneham utsṛjya gacchanti bāṣpapūrṇāvilekṣaṇāḥ
english: "Having abandoned him here, the kinsmen do not remain beside their beloved kinsman; casting off their love, they go away, their eyes brimming and clouded with tears."

sanskrit: prājño vā yadi vā mūrkhaḥ sadhano nirdhano 'pi vā sarvaḥ kālavaśaṃ yāti śubhāśubhasamanvitaḥ
english: "Wise man or fool, rich man or poor — every one, endowed with his good and his evil, passes into the power of Time."

sanskrit: kiṃ kariṣyatha śocitvā mṛtaṃ kim anuśocatha sarvasya hi prabhuḥ kālo dharmataḥ samadarśanaḥ
english: "What will you gain by grieving? Why do you mourn the dead? For Time is the lord of all, looking upon all alike according to the law."

sanskrit: yauvanasthāṃś ca bālāṃś ca vṛddhān garbhagatān api sarvān āviśate mṛtyur evaṃbhūtam idaṃ jagat
english: "Those in the prime of youth, and children, and the aged, and even those yet in the womb — all of them death enters. Such is this world."

sanskrit: jambuka uvāca aho mandīkṛtaḥ sneho gṛdhreṇehālpamedhasā putrasnehābhibhūtānāṃ yuṣmākaṃ śocatāṃ bhṛśam
english: The jackal said: Ah, by this dull-witted vulture the love of you, who are overcome by tenderness for your son and grieve so sorely, has been made to grow cold!

sanskrit: samaiḥ samyak prayuktaiś ca vacanaiḥ praśrayottaraiḥ yad gacchatha jalasthāyaṃ sneham utsṛjya dustyajam
english: "By words measured and well-marshalled, couched in courtesy, has he persuaded you to depart at the setting of the sun, casting off a love so hard to cast off?"

sanskrit: aho putraviyogena mṛtaśūnyopasevanāt krośatāṃ vai bhṛśaṃ duḥkhaṃ vivatsānāṃ gavām iva
english: "Ah, in the loss of a son, in the tending of the dead and desolate, how grievous is the anguish of those who cry aloud — like cows bereft of their calves!"

sanskrit: adya śokaṃ vijānāmi mānuṣāṇāṃ mahītale snehaṃ hi karuṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā mamāpy aśrūṇy athāgaman
english: "This day I learn the grief of men upon the earth; for beholding their piteous love, tears come even to my eyes."

sanskrit: yatno hi satataṃ kāryaḥ kṛto daivena sidhyati daivaṃ puruṣakāraś ca kṛtāntenopapadyate
english: "Effort must ever be made; once made, it is brought to fulfillment by destiny. Destiny and human exertion alike are wrought together by Fate."

sanskrit: anirvedaḥ sadā kāryo nirvedād dhi kutaḥ sukham prayatnāt prāpyate hy arthaḥ kasmād gacchatha nirdayāḥ
english: "One must never yield to despair, for from despair whence comes happiness? By striving the object is attained; why then do you go away so heartlessly?"

sanskrit: ātmamāṃsopavṛttaṃ ca śarīrārdhamayīṃ tanuṃ pitṝṇāṃ vaṃśakartāraṃ vane tyaktvā kva yāsyatha
english: "This body, sprung from your own flesh, formed of half your own frame, the continuer of the line of your fathers — having forsaken it in the forest, where will you go?"

sanskrit: atha vāstaṃ gate sūrye saṃdhyākāla upasthite tato neṣyatha vā putram ihasthā vā bhaviṣyatha
english: "When the sun has set and twilight is come, then you may bear away your son, or else remain here."

sanskrit: gṛdhra uvāca adya varṣasahasraṃ me sāgraṃ jātasya mānuṣāḥ na ca paśyāmi jīvantaṃ mṛtaṃ strīpuṃnapuṃsakam
english: The vulture said: Now a full thousand years and more have passed since I was born, O men, yet I have never seen one — woman, man, or eunuch — once dead come back to life.

sanskrit: mṛtā garbheṣu jāyante mriyante jātamātrakāḥ vikramanto mriyante ca yauvanasthās tathāpare
english: "Some die in the womb; some are born and die the moment they are born; others die while striding forth in their strength, and yet others in the bloom of youth."

sanskrit: anityānīha bhāgyāni catuṣpāt pakṣiṇām api jaṅgamājaṅgamānāṃ cāpy āyur agre 'vatiṣṭhate
english: "Fortunes here are fleeting, for four-footed creatures and for birds; and for things that move and things that move not, life-span stands ever at its very end."

sanskrit: iṣṭadāraviyuktāś ca putraśokānvitās tathā dahyamānāḥ sma śokena gṛhaṃ gacchanti nityadā
english: "Sundered from beloved wives, and stricken with grief for sons, men, ever burning with sorrow, go home day after day."

sanskrit: aniṣṭānāṃ sahasrāṇi tatheṣṭānāṃ śatāni ca utsṛjyeha prayātā vai bāndhavā bhṛśaduḥkhitāḥ
english: "Thousands of things unwished, and hundreds of things wished-for, the kinsmen here forsake and go their way, plunged in deep sorrow."

sanskrit: tyajyatām eṣa nistejāḥ śūnyaḥ kāṣṭhatvam āgataḥ anyadehaviṣakto hi śāvaṃ kāṣṭham upāsate
english: "Let this lifeless thing be abandoned, empty, reduced to the state of a log. For one whose self has passed into another body, the corpse is but a log to wait upon."

sanskrit: bhrāntajīvasya vai bāṣpaṃ kasmād dhitvā na gacchatha nirarthako hy ayaṃ sneho nirarthaś ca parigrahaḥ
english: "For him whose life has wandered away, why do you not lay aside your tears and go? For this love is fruitless, and fruitless too is this clinging."

sanskrit: na cakṣurbhyāṃ na karṇābhyāṃ saṃśṛṇoti samīkṣate tasmād enaṃ samutsṛjya svagṛhān gacchatāśu vai
english: "Not with eyes, not with ears, does he hear or behold any longer; therefore abandon him and go quickly to your own homes."

sanskrit: mokṣadharmāśritair vākyair hetumadbhir aniṣṭhuraiḥ mayoktā gacchata kṣipraṃ svaṃ svam eva niveśanam
english: "By words grounded in the law of liberation, well-reasoned and not unkind, I have spoken to you: go quickly, each to his own dwelling."

sanskrit: prajñāvijñānayuktena buddhisaṃjñāpradāyinā vacanaṃ śrāvitā rūkṣaṃ mānuṣāḥ saṃnivartata
english: "With words endowed with wisdom and discernment, words that bring back understanding and reason, you, O men, have been told this hard truth: turn back!"

sanskrit: jambuka uvāca imaṃ kanakavarṇābhaṃ bhūṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaṃ gṛdhravākyāt kathaṃ putraṃ tyajadhvaṃ pitṛpiṇḍadam
english: The jackal said: This boy, hued like burnished gold, adorned with ornaments — how, at a vulture's word, will you abandon a son who would offer the funeral rice to your fathers?

sanskrit: na snehasya virodho 'sti vilāparuditasya vai mṛtasyāsya parityāgāt tāpo vai bhavitā dhruvam
english: "There is no resisting the love that weeps and wails aloud; from abandoning this dead one, anguish will surely come to you."

sanskrit: śrūyate śambuke śūdre hate brāhmaṇadārakaḥ jīvito dharmam āsādya rāmāt satyaparākramāt
english: "It is heard that when Śambūka, the Śūdra, was slain, a Brāhmaṇa's child was restored to life through righteousness, by Rāma whose valor is truth."

sanskrit: tathā śvetasya rājarṣer bālo diṣṭāntam āgataḥ śvo 'bhūte dharmanityena mṛtaḥ saṃjīvitaḥ punaḥ
english: "And so too the child of the royal sage Śveta, who had reached his appointed end — at break of day, dead though he was, he was restored to life again by one ever devoted to righteousness."

sanskrit: tathā kaś cid bhavet siddho munir vā devatāpi vā kṛpaṇānām anukrośaṃ kuryād vo rudatām iha
english: "Even so, some perfected sage, or holy man, or even a deity, might take pity on you wretched ones weeping here."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity uktāḥ saṃnyavartanta śokārtāḥ putravatsalāḥ aṅke śiraḥ samādhāya rurudur bahuvistaram
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed, the grieving folk, tender toward their son, turned back, and laying his head upon their laps, they wept long and without restraint.

sanskrit: gṛdhra uvāca aśrupātapariklinnaḥ pāṇisparśanapīḍitaḥ dharmarājaprayogāc ca dīrghāṃ nidrāṃ praveśitaḥ
english: The vulture said: Drenched with the fall of your tears, pressed by the touch of your hands, and by the working of the King of Righteousness, he has been led into a long sleep.

sanskrit: tapasāpi hi saṃyukto na kāle nopahanyate sarvasnehāvasānaṃ tad idaṃ tat pretapattanam
english: "Even one joined with austerity is not, before his time, struck down. This is that place where all loves come to their end — the city of the dead."

sanskrit: bālavṛddhasahasrāṇi sadā saṃtyajya bāndhavāḥ dināni caiva rātrīś ca duḥkhaṃ tiṣṭhanti bhūtale
english: "Forsaking always thousands of children and aged ones, the kinsmen abide in sorrow upon the earth, through the days and through the nights."

sanskrit: alaṃ nirbandham āgamya śokasya parivāraṇam apratyayaṃ kuto hy asya punar adyeha jīvitam
english: "Enough of this stubbornness! Let the hindrance of grief be put away. There is no warrant for it: whence should this child have life again here today?"

sanskrit: naiṣa jambukavākyena punaḥ prāpsyati jīvitam mṛtasyotsṛṣṭadehasya punar deho na vidyate
english: "Not by the jackal's words will this one regain his life; for the dead, whose body has been cast off, there is no body again."

sanskrit: na vai mūrtipradānena na jambukaśatair api śakyo jīvayituṃ hy eṣa bālo varṣaśatair api
english: "Neither by the giving of a body, nor even by a hundred jackals, can this child be made to live — no, not in a hundred years."

sanskrit: api rudraḥ kumāro vā brahmā vā viṣṇur eva vā varam asmai prayaccheyus tato jīved ayaṃ śiśuḥ
english: "Were Rudra, or Kumāra, or Brahmā, or Viṣṇu himself to grant him a boon — then might this infant live."

sanskrit: na ca bāṣpavimokṣeṇa na cāśvāsakṛtena vai na dīrgharuditeneha punarjīvo bhaviṣyati
english: "Not by the shedding of tears, not by any comforting, not by long weeping here, will he come to life again."

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca kroṣṭukaś caiva yūyaṃ caivāsya bāndhavāḥ dharmādharmau gṛhītveha sarve vartāmahe 'dhvani
english: "I, and this jackal too, and you, his kinsmen — all of us, having taken up our righteousness and unrighteousness, are journeying here upon the road."

sanskrit: apriyaṃ paruṣaṃ cāpi paradrohaṃ parastriyam adharmam anṛtaṃ caiva dūrāt prājño nivartayet
english: "From what is unkind and harsh, from injury to others and from another's wife, from unrighteousness and falsehood, let the wise man hold himself far aloof."

sanskrit: satyaṃ dharmaṃ śubhaṃ nyāyyaṃ prāṇināṃ mahatīṃ dayām ajihmatvam aśāṭhyaṃ ca yatnataḥ parimārgata
english: "Truth, righteousness, goodness, what is just, great compassion for living beings, uprightness and freedom from guile — seek these out with diligence."

sanskrit: mātaraṃ pitaraṃ caiva bāndhavān suhṛdas tathā jīvato ye na paśyanti teṣāṃ dharmaviparyayaḥ
english: "Those who, while their mother and father, their kinsmen and friends, are still alive, take no heed of them — for such men there is a perversion of duty."

sanskrit: yo na paśyati cakṣurbhyāṃ neṅgate ca kathaṃ cana tasya niṣṭhāvasānānte rudantaḥ kiṃ kariṣyatha
english: "For one who no longer sees with his eyes, nor stirs in any way at all, who has reached the end of his appointed course — what will you accomplish by weeping?"

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity uktās taṃ sutaṃ tyaktvā bhūmau śokapariplutāḥ dahyamānāḥ sutasnehāt prayayur bāndhavā gṛhān
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed, the kinsmen, leaving that son upon the ground, overwhelmed with grief and burning with love for their child, set out for their homes.

sanskrit: jambuka uvāca dāruṇo martyaloko 'yaṃ sarvaprāṇivināśanaḥ iṣṭabandhuviyogaś ca tathaivālpaṃ ca jīvitam
english: The jackal said: Dreadful is this world of mortals, the destroyer of all living things, with its parting from beloved kin, and life withal so brief.

sanskrit: bahv alīkam asatyaṃ ca prativādāpriyaṃvadam imaṃ prekṣya punarbhāvaṃ duḥkhaśokābhivardhanam
english: "Full of falsehood and untruth, of contradiction and unwelcome speech — beholding this state of recurring birth, which swells the tide of pain and grief —"

sanskrit: na me mānuṣaloko 'yaṃ muhūrtam api rocate aho dhig gṛdhravākyena saṃnivartatha mānuṣāḥ
english: "this world of men pleases me not even for a moment. Ah, shame, that at a vulture's word you turn away, O men!"

sanskrit: pradīptāḥ putraśokena yathaivābuddhayas tathā kathaṃ gacchatha sasnehāḥ sutasnehaṃ visṛjya ca śrutvā gṛdhrasya vacanaṃ pāpasyehākṛtātmanaḥ
english: "Ablaze with grief for your son as you are, you are likewise become senseless. How can you, with your tenderness, go away, casting off love for your son, having heeded the words of that wicked, unrefined vulture?"

sanskrit: sukhasyānantaraṃ duḥkhaṃ duḥkhasyānantaraṃ sukham sukhaduḥkhānvite loke nehāsty ekam anantakam
english: "Hard upon joy follows sorrow, and hard upon sorrow follows joy; in a world compounded of joy and sorrow, no single thing here is without an end."

sanskrit: imaṃ kṣititale nyasya bālaṃ rūpasamanvitaṃ kulaśokākaraṃ mūḍhāḥ putraṃ tyaktvā kva yāsyatha
english: "Having laid this comely child upon the ground — a son whose loss would be the wellspring of grief to your line — where, you fools, will you go, abandoning him?"

sanskrit: rūpayauvanasaṃpannaṃ dyotamānam iva śriyā jīvantam enaṃ paśyāmi manasā nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: "Endowed with beauty and youth, as though shining with splendor — I see him living, with my mind's eye; of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: vināśaś cāpy anarho 'sya sukhaṃ prāpsyatha mānuṣāḥ putraśokāgnidagdhānāṃ mṛtam apy adya vaḥ kṣamam
english: "Destruction is not his desert; you shall yet find happiness, O men. For you, consumed by the fire of grief for your son, that he should even be dead would today be a mercy to you."

sanskrit: duḥkhasaṃbhāvanāṃ kṛtvā dhārayitvā svayaṃ sukhaṃ tyaktvā gamiṣyatha kvādya samutsṛjyālpabuddhivat
english: "Having brought sorrow upon yourselves, and holding fast to your own ease, where will you go this day, abandoning him, forsaking him like men of little wit?"

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tathā dharmavirodhena priyamithyābhidhyāyinā śmaśānavāsinā nityaṃ rātriṃ mṛgayatā tadā
english: Bhīṣma said: And so, by the jackal — opposed to righteousness, brooding upon false endearments, a dweller in the cremation ground, ever ranging by night —

sanskrit: tato madhyasthatāṃ nītā vacanair amṛtopamaiḥ jambukena svakāryārthaṃ bāndhavās tasya dhiṣṭhitāḥ
english: the kinsmen were brought to wavering irresolution by words that seemed like nectar; by the jackal, for his own ends, were they held fast there.

sanskrit: gṛdhra uvāca ayaṃ pretasamākīrṇo yakṣarākṣasasevitaḥ dāruṇaḥ kānanoddeśaḥ kauśikair abhināditaḥ
english: The vulture said: This dreadful tract of forest is thronged with ghosts, haunted by Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, and made to resound with the cries of owls.

sanskrit: bhīmaḥ sughoraś ca tathā nīlameghasamaprabhaḥ asmiñ śavaṃ parityajya pretakāryāṇy upāsata
english: "Fearful and most terrible it is, dark as a blue-black cloud. Lay down the corpse in this place and perform the rites for the dead."

sanskrit: bhānur yāvan na yāty astaṃ yāvac ca vimalā diśaḥ tāvad enaṃ parityajya pretakāryāṇy upāsata
english: "While the sun has not yet gone to its setting, and while the quarters of the sky are still clear, lay him down and attend to the funeral rites."

sanskrit: nadanti paruṣaṃ śyenāḥ śivāḥ krośanti dāruṇāḥ mṛgendrāḥ pratinandanti ravir astaṃ ca gacchati
english: "Harshly the hawks are screaming, the dreadful jackals howl, the lions of the wild answer back in chorus — and the sun is going down to its setting."
